amp.model: Vox AC30 (clean verse) / Fender Bassman for the heavier chorus layers

rig.cab: Vox AC30 stock 2x12 with Celestion Blues
rig.notes: The Small Clone is the entire identity of this tone — depth switch up, rate slow, running into a clean amp for the verse, with the DS-1 stacked on top for the chorus and solo. The album take is a full whole step down to D standard; Nirvana usually played it live only a half step down (Eb standard), which sits a semitone above the record. [Sourcing: widely-reported]

title: In Bloom

rig.notes: Two distinct guitar tones: the tighter Mesa/Boogie preamp voice on the verses and the fatter Bassman for the layered choruses, so build the song from two amp/gain states rather than one. A ProCo RAT was on the Nevermind sessions (sometimes split to a DI into the console) but per-song use is not documented — treat it as the optional darker-flavoured alternative to the DS-1 here. [Sourcing: widely-reported]

rig.notes: There is essentially no rig here: the tone is a nearly-unplayable detuned pawn-shop acoustic captured very quietly and then built around, so dynamics and a soft touch matter far more than gear.
